I'm testing the Dell 32-inch UltraSharp U3226Q, and my impressions so far are very positive. The picture quality on this OLED panel is impressive, especially with HDR enabled in macOS. I'll be posting a full hands-on review of the UltraSharp on our YouTube channel.

On a related note, I want to highlight an important improvement Apple has made to HDR support in macOS 27. Previously, when using macOS 26 Tahoe with a third-party HDR-capable display, one drawback was the inability to enable HDR at the popular 2560 x 1440 scaled resolution. Fortunately, the latest version of macOS has addressed this issue.

The Problem

If you're using a third-party HDR10-capable display with macOS Tahoe, you'll see an HDR toggle under Settings → Displays. When you switch it on, HDR content becomes viewable. You can see an example in the screenshot below.

But notice in the same screenshot that I'm running at 1920 x 1080, which is exactly the result of doubling the pixel count from this 4K UHD display's native 3840 x 2160 resolution.

Most users probably don't want to use 1920 x 1080, because on a 4K display it makes everything look too large. The Dell Ultrasharp U3226Q is a 32-inch display, so running at 1920 x 1080 would significantly reduce the available screen real estate.

The fix in macOS is simple: just select a scaled resolution, such as the very common 2560 x 1440 (which is also the default for Apple's 5K Studio Display). The issue is that in macOS Tahoe, once you select a scaled resolution, HDR gets disabled. Take a look at the screenshot below:

As you can see, the HDR toggle is gone, and macOS automatically switches back to Standard Dynamic Range (SDR). This means that when using an HDR display with macOS Tahoe, you have to choose between HDR and your preferred scaled resolution.

Fortunately, this has been fixed in macOS 27 Golden Gate. In the screenshot below, you can see that scaled resolution and HDR can now be selected and used simultaneously. This is a built-in system option, with no third-party software required.

So if you're using a third-party HDR display, this alone, in my opinion, makes it worth upgrading from macOS Tahoe to macOS Golden Gate. Of course, I was testing on my M4 MacBook Pro. I tried doing the same on my M1 Max MacBook Pro, but I couldn't select both options simultaneously, even though it's also running macOS 27, so it appears there are some hardware limitations as well.

macOS Golden Gate includes a range of new features, which I've covered in my Siri AI overview, my top macOS features video, and my macOS 27 final review. One feature related to HDR displays is that macOS 27 now offers more comprehensive native HDR support across the entire system.

You'll notice brighter highlights, brighter cursors, and higher overall contrast compared to the spectrum offered by macOS Tahoe. Whether you're an Apple Studio Display XDR user, a Pro Display XDR user, or using a third-party OLED display, the visual experience is outstanding.

What do you think? Would you pair a third-party external display with your Mac? If so, would you consider using an HDR-capable display?
